newsitem.title: USA: Enron, PGE meeting with Ore. delayed a week.
newsitem.headline: Enron, PGE meeting with Ore. delayed a week.

text.p: The latest round of settlement talks between staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC), Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co has been delayed to March 12, Enron said Wednesday.
The parties were scheduled to meet Thursday afternoon in Salem, but illness of a key Oregon staff member led to the postponement.
Two previous rounds of negotiations on terms of the planned merger of Enron and Portland General have been held, but the issue of a rate cut for Oregon customers remains a sticking point.
The OPUC staff has called for a $189.6 million rate cut over four years after a merger, while the companies' last offer was $40 to $50 million.
Enron and Portland General submitted a revised settlement to the staff last Thursday, the OPUC said.
The OPUC had set March 17 as a deadline for final decision on the merger, but that timeframe now looks "virtually impossible," said the Enron spokesman.
